rationale: M60 XML deep review, finding X10. XML Schema's `QName` datatype carries the `collapse` whiteSpace facet (XSD 1.0 3.3.13), so a QName-typed attribute value has its whitespace runs collapsed and its ends trimmed BEFORE it is read as a name. The analyzer did not, so `type="CT_GeoHierarchyEntity "` — a trailing space, written by a human and legal, because XML only normalises tab and newline in an attribute value and leaves inner spaces alone — failed the QName parse and the reference was REFUSED. One site in the corpus, in office_drawing_2014_chartex.xsd, where a complex type declared 7 lines above went unreferenced because of one character. Four spellings are pinned because the facet distinguishes them: trailing, leading, and a double run on both ends all collapse to the same name, and `CT_ Target` does NOT — collapse replaces a run with ONE space, and an interior space makes the value not a QName at all, so that reference must still be refused. A fixture that only pinned the trailing-space case would pass against a fix that simply trimmed the ends, which accepts a different and wrong set of values. `clean` is the control, and the three collapsed spellings collapsing onto ONE target is itself pinned: three elements declaring the same type is three references, and the graph must say so through `occurrences` rather than losing two of them to the dedupe. The facet is applied ONCE, where the value enters the candidate queue, because the deferred pass re-parses `candidate.value` — applying it at the parse site alone passed the push-site check and then failed the deferred one, and the edge was refused exactly as before, which is the shape of a fix that appears to work and does not.

forbidRelationships.note: collapse replaces a whitespace RUN with ONE space and trims the ENDS; it does not remove an interior space, so `CT_ Target` is not a QName and no reference may be derived from it. This clause is what separates the facet from a trim.
nor may the value be split on the space and one half published — a reference target is a NAME, and half a name is not one

forbidSymbols.name: CT_
forbidSymbols.note: the half-name on either side of the interior space must not become a symbol; publishing it would put a truncated declaration in the graph

_targetSpelling: THE SAME-FILE TIER (2026-10-12): a target this file declares under EXACTLY ONE owner is emitted as `Owner.name` — the two-part identity the analyzer already computes (`qualifiedName = ownerName + '.' + name`) and which `parallel-indexer.ts:3435-3437` already looks up — so the store binds it without a store change. The bare name stays in `metadata.bareTarget`. A target the file declares under ZERO or 2+ owners is left exactly as it was.
